sections.title: Executive investment summary: a cash-rich Indian PCR-kit maker priced for growth it has not shown

blocks.text: [F] 3B BlackBio Dx (formerly Kilpest India) designs, manufactures and sells real-time PCR (qPCR) diagnostic kits under the TRUPCR brand, plus rapid lateral-flow tests, NGS kits, digital PCR assays and extraction kits, from a single Indian plant at Govindpura, Bhopal (AR2026 p.100, p.96). [F] A legacy agrochemicals division (pesticides, micro and bio-fertilisers, larvicides) still sits inside the listed company and sold Rs 10.80 cr in FY26 against Rs 131.12 cr for diagnostics (AR2026 p.138). [F] Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 141.92 cr, PBT Rs 76.97 cr and PAT Rs 59.93 cr (AR2026 p.27).

[F] The group has three operating legs: the Indian parent (standalone diagnostics sales Rs 86.48 cr, AR2026 p.101); TRUPCR Europe Ltd, a 70%-owned Manchester distributor/finisher of TRUPCR kits (turnover Rs 20.70 cr, AOC-1, AR2026 p.57); and Coris BioConcept, a Belgian lateral-flow maker focused on antimicrobial resistance (AMR) tests, acquired on 29 August 2025 and consolidated for seven months (turnover Rs 35.91 cr, AR2026 p.57). [MC] The company earns money by selling kits to distributors at an average of about Rs 700-800 per kit; distributors mark up 15-20% and labs charge patients roughly Rs 2,000-2,500 per test (CALL Jun 2026).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation already assumes a different company. [F] The reverse DCF requires ~37.2% annual sales growth for five years versus 8.8% in the base case; every DCF scenario (bear Rs 451.8, base Rs 596.2, bull Rs 732.8 per share) sits 52-70% below the Rs 1,520 price (NUMBERS).

2. Organic growth has stalled. [F] Standalone diagnostics sales grew only 10.4% in FY26 (AR2026 p.101) and standalone domestic diagnostics only 6.1% (Rs 61.31 cr to Rs 65.07 cr, AR2026 p.129) [E]; [MC] management cut FY26 guidance from 15-20% (CALL Aug 2025) to 10-15% (CALL Feb 2026).

3. Export growth was intra-group. [F] Standalone diagnostics exports rose Rs 17.04 cr to Rs 21.41 cr, but sales to the TPE subsidiary rose Rs 7.55 cr to Rs 11.86 cr (AR2026 p.129, p.161); [E] exports to third parties were roughly flat at about Rs 9.5 cr in both years.

4. FY26 profit quality is lower than the headline. [F] Consolidated other income of Rs 25.56 cr includes Rs 7.82 cr 'credit to P&L for self-constructed assets' and Rs 3.00 cr of subsidies (AR2026 p.156); [E] stripping these leaves FY26 PBT of about Rs 66 cr, only ~3% above FY25's Rs 64 cr.

5. Margins have collapsed post-acquisition. [F] Operating margin was 23.96% in Q4 FY26 and 25.44% in Q1 FY27, against 52% in FY25 (NUMBERS); [F] Q1 FY27 PAT fell 29% YoY despite revenue +50.7% (NUMBERS).

6. Coris is structurally loss-making outside HAT orders. [MC] Coris had a 12-month EBITDA loss of EUR 325k (CALL Feb 2026) and management expects Coris losses in Q1-Q2 FY27 before the HAT quarter (CALL Jun 2026); [MC] HAT is a finite EUR 6m, four-year Congo-linked contract (CALL Feb 2026).

7. Receivables are stretching. [F] Standalone receivables rose 22.8% to Rs 43.20 cr while standalone revenue rose 7.45% (AR2026 p.121, p.105); [MC] management is matching competitors' 4-5 month credit terms (CALL Feb 2026).

8. Accounting presentation is internally inconsistent. [F] CARO states no loans to subsidiaries while the balance sheet shows a Rs 3.12 cr loan to TPE (AR2026 p.115, p.127); notes cite pre-Ind AS standards (AS-17/18/20/21) while auditors opine on Ind AS (AR2026 p.158-160, p.140); no goodwill or purchase-price allocation for Coris is disclosed.

9. Distribution and related-party opacity. [MC] An individual holding 5.14% of the equity (AR2026 p.96) is described by management as the company's exclusive Indian channel partner since 2013, and is no longer shown as a related party (CALL Aug 2025); the share of sales routed through this partner is not disclosed.

10. Family-run board with rising pay. [F] Three of six directors are one family, the CFO is a promoter on the audit committee, and executive pay rose 29.03% against a 9.37% median employee rise (AR2026 p.67, p.71, p.76).

Is FY26 the new base or a high-water mark? [AI] Bulls read Rs 142 cr revenue as a platform for 15-20% growth (CALL Jun 2026 [MC]); the last two quarters (Rs 35.4 cr and Rs 33.5 cr at ~24-25% operating margin, NUMBERS [F]) suggest the market may be capitalising an annualised HAT-boosted year.

Is the treasury an asset or a temptation? [AI] Rs 258 cr of liquid assets [E] could be value-accretive if deployed at the 6-8x multiples management says are 'normal' (CALL Jun 2026 [MC]); but the first deal bought a loss-making business and management is now widening its search beyond hard-core IVD (CALL Jun 2026 [MC]).

Is the Indian franchise moat-protected? [MC] Management cites lab validation stickiness and multiplex panels (CALL Feb 2026); [AI] the market may be underestimating how much growth now depends on credit terms and price-matching in a Rs 500-600 cr niche where the company already claims 12-15%.

Could the market be too negative on Coris? [MC] A EUR 1.41m HAT order for Dec 2026 is confirmed and RESIST-5 IVDR certification is in hand (PPT Sep 2026); [AI] if US FDA clearance arrives, a loss-making asset could become a modest contributor, which the base DCF does not credit.

Is the DCF too harsh? [AI] Our DCF excludes the treasury and other income from equity value (NUMBERS method note); that understates value, but [E] the treasury is far smaller than the Rs 675 cr gap between the market cap and the bull-case equity value.

blocks.text: [AI] The market appears to price 3B BlackBio as a high-growth diagnostics platform; our reading of the filings is of a mature, high-margin Indian kit business growing high single digits, a UK distributor that mostly re-sells the parent's kits, and a sub-scale Belgian acquisition whose seven-month profit leaned on a tender order, R&D capitalisation booked as other income and subsidies. [F] At Rs 1,520 the stock trades at 23.3x trailing earnings and 24.7x EV/EBITDA, with ~34% of PBT from other income (NUMBERS). [AI] The variant view is that the investment case rests almost entirely on capital allocation of the treasury, not on the operating business, and that is not a case the current valuation discounts for execution risk.

blocks.text: [F] The AR states Coris was acquired by '3B (70%) along with its UK subsidiary TPE' and the investment schedule shows '9% shares in Coris by minority' (AR2026 p.31, p.154). [AI] This implies 3B holds 70% directly and TPE 30%, giving an effective group interest of about 91%, with the TPE minority shareholders indirectly owning ~9% of Coris; the identity of TPE's 30% minority is not disclosed, though TPE director Harminder Singh is listed as a related party (AR2026 p.83).

[AI] The listed entity is 54 years old, but the diagnostics business as investors now see it is young: the JV was folded into the listed company only after the amalgamation order, TPE became a subsidiary in March 2022, the first earnings call was August 2025 and the first acquisition closed in August 2025. [F] Pre-COVID revenue was Rs 29 cr in FY20 (NUMBERS). [AI] The post-COVID franchise has therefore only three to four years of clean history, and the consolidated group in its current form has three reported quarters with Coris for the full period.

sections.title: Business model: from assay design to a distributor's shelf

items: Step 1 - Assay R&D: [MC] 1-1.5 years to optimise amplification targets and master mixes; multi-tube panels take about two years (CALL Aug 2025). [F] FY26 R&D spend Rs 3.41 cr (3.51% of turnover), of which Rs 1.13 cr capitalised (AR2026 p.66).
Step 2 - Regulatory approval: [F] CDSCO licences in India; CE-IVD/IVDR in Europe with BSI as notified body; country registrations take 10-15 months (AR2026 p.29, p.103).

Step 3 - Manufacture: [MC] all 3B kits are made in Bhopal with Indian staff; 'most' raw materials sourced in India (CALL Aug 2025). [F] Diagnostics raw-material imports were Rs 5.95 cr, about 38% of diagnostics material consumed (AR2026 p.134) [E].
Step 4 - UK finishing: [MC] bulk kits are transferred to TPE and finished in Manchester for 'Made in UK' supply with same-time-zone support (CALL Feb 2026).

Step 5 - Selling: [MC] demo and validation in the customer's lab, then price negotiation; onboarding takes 3-6 months (CALL Aug 2025). [MC] Sales through distributors at Rs 700-800 per kit on average (CALL Jun 2026).
Step 6 - Lock-in: [MC] reagent-rental contracts place instruments with labs for 3-5 years on condition only TRUPCR assays are used; over 15 such contracts (PPT Sep 2026).

blocks.text: [E] In the standalone business, diagnostics material cost was 18.1% of diagnostics sales in FY26 (Rs 15.65 cr on Rs 86.48 cr, AR2026 p.134), implying a materials-only gross margin above 80%. [F] Standalone operating margin was 54.67% (AR2026 p.136). [AI] Value is captured at the assay-design and regulatory-dossier stage: the physical inputs are cheap, and the price reflects validated performance, menu breadth and support. [MC] Management attributes the margin advantage to low Indian manpower and overhead costs rather than pricing power (CALL Aug 2025), which also explains why Coris, with Belgian salaries, earns far less.

[AI] Downstream, distributors and labs capture a large share of the end-test price: on management's numbers a Rs 700-800 kit becomes a Rs 2,000-2,500 test (CALL Jun 2026 [MC]). The company does not own the patient relationship.

[F] Consolidated net fixed assets were only Rs 7 cr from FY23 to FY25 on revenue of Rs 62-96 cr (NUMBERS). [F] The FY26 jump to Rs 28 cr reflects consolidation of Coris and Rs 7.82 cr of self-constructed (capitalised R&D) assets credited to income (AR2026 p.147, p.156). [MC] Instruments for sample-to-answer are OEM-sourced rather than developed (CALL Feb 2026). [AI] The Indian business is asset-light; the group has become somewhat heavier with Coris, mainly through capitalised development cost rather than plant.

[MC] HAT supply depends on Congo, where war and Ebola may delay offtake (CALL Jun 2026).

[F] All Indian manufacturing is at one plant in Govindpura, Bhopal (AR2026 p.96); [AI] a single-site disruption would hit the highest-margin part of the group, and no business-interruption cover is quantified beyond a general insurance statement (AR2026 p.44).

blocks.text: [F] Our model's year-5 sales range from Rs 186.5 cr (bear) to Rs 284.4 cr (bull) (NUMBERS). [AI] Outside the model, the realistic upside path is acquisition-led: one or two European or US IVD acquisitions with the treasury, US clearance for RESIST-5, and IVDR-certified TRUPCR. The downside path is a mature Indian kit business with a treasury earning deposit rates and a marginal Belgian subsidiary. Both paths are plausible; only the first is consistent with the current price.

sections.title: Research view

blocks.text: [F] At Rs 1,520 the share price sits above every scenario in our model: the bear, base and bull values of Rs 451.8, Rs 596.2 and Rs 732.8 are 70.3%, 60.8% and 51.8% below the price (NUMBERS). [AI] The gap is driven by the market capitalising management's growth narrative and the optionality of a large treasury, while our model capitalises the observed organic business and excludes the treasury. The treasury explains part of the gap; it does not explain most of it.

summary.one_line: 3B BlackBio Dx is a debt-free, cash-rich Indian PCR-kit maker with a stable ~55% standalone margin, but its FY26 growth came mostly from the Coris acquisition and non-operating income, margins fell to ~25% in the last two quarters, and the Rs 1,520 price implies ~37% annual growth for five years - more than double even the bull case in our model.
bull_points: [F] Net-cash balance sheet: cash, bank balances and investments of about Rs 258 cr [E] against borrowings of Rs 3 cr (AR2026 p.147; NUMBERS), funding M&A without dilution.
[F] The Indian kit franchise earns a stable standalone operating margin of 54.67% (FY25 55.07%) with diagnostics material cost only ~18% of sales [E] (AR2026 p.134, p.136).
[F] TRUPCR Europe grew from GBP 0.45m (FY23) to GBP 1.75m (FY26) and is profitable (AR2026 p.102, p.57).
[MC] A EUR 1.41m HAT order is confirmed for December 2026, larger than the ~EUR 0.81-0.85m of HAT revenue consolidated in FY26 (PPT Sep 2026; CALL Feb 2026).
[MC] IVDR transition with BSI and a US FDA filing for Coris's RESIST-5 offer regulatory upside from FY28 (AR2026 p.29-30; CALL Jun 2026).
bear_points: [F] The reverse DCF implies 37.2% annual sales growth for five years versus 8.8% in the base case; bear/base/bull values of Rs 451.8/596.2/732.8 are 52-70% below the Rs 1,520 price (NUMBERS).

[E] Organic growth is ~10%: standalone diagnostics +10.4% and domestic diagnostics +6.1% in FY26, while third-party exports were flat at ~Rs 9.5 cr once intra-group sales to TPE are removed (AR2026 p.101, p.129, p.161).

[F] FY26 other income of Rs 25.56 cr (34% of PBT) included Rs 7.82 cr non-cash credit for self-constructed assets and Rs 3.00 cr subsidies (AR2026 p.156; NUMBERS); [E] PBT excluding these grew only ~3%.
[F] Consolidated operating margin was 24.0% in Q4 FY26 and 25.4% in Q1 FY27 versus 52% in FY25; Q1 FY27 PAT fell 29% YoY (NUMBERS).

[F] The audited annual report contradicts itself: CARO says no loans to subsidiaries while the balance sheet shows a Rs 3.12 cr loan to TPE, notes cite pre-Ind AS standards, and no Coris purchase-price allocation is disclosed (AR2026 p.115, p.127, p.158).
